title: Migration apply: releaseIdBlock can throw inside the failure path, masking the original error and leaving the block reserved for its 7-day TTL (QCLI-520 round-2 findings N1-N7, ordered)
description:
Findings from the QCLI-520 round-2 FULL review (unit quest-cli-review-659r2, model deepseek-flash, DEC-183 Stage 1), which APPROVED opum-ai/quest-cli#659 at 1c77a30d (merged as 96de7c59). All seven are MINOR or NIT; none reopens a round-1 item. ITEMS ARE IN RANK ORDER, N1 HIGHEST.

N1 (MINOR, highest): releaseIdBlock can throw IdAllocationLockTimeoutError at backlog-public.ts:1094, :1107 and :1123 -- inside the very paths that exist to record a failure. That masks the original error, converts the conflict and source-fingerprint paths from returning a failed receipt into throwing, and leaves the block reserved, which is the 7-day leak MAJOR-3 closed for the success path. Fix: give each release its own try/catch; rethrow the ORIGINAL error with the release failure as its cause; keep returning the failed receipt on the conflict and fingerprint paths; use separate tries for the task and milestone releases so one failure cannot skip the other.

N2 (MINOR): releaseIdBlock matches id + family only (id-allocation.ts:694-702), never at or a run identity, though the note describes the match as id, at and family. Have reserve hand back the entries it wrote, or a run id, and match on that.

N3 (MINOR): the error an operator usually meets is migration_approval_digest_mismatch (validation, no hint; backlog-public.ts:889-890, main.ts:4949-4971), not migration_id_block_moved. Add the re-preview hint to that mapping, leaving the exit code unchanged, and name both errors in the CHANGELOG and the guide.

N4 (MINOR): releaseIdBlock has no unit test of its own. Cover a same-family entry with another id surviving, another family entry surviving, and a null commonDirectory being a false no-op that writes nothing.

N5 (NIT): the lock-timeout hint says Retry the create (main.ts:4872) but is now reachable from migration.

N6 (NIT): the task record-directory list is duplicated (backlog-public.ts:760-761 and main.ts:1358).

N7 (NIT): main.ts:2502-2504 hardcodes "M" and ignores the marker parameter.

Not to be worked until the day plan names it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every release on a failure path runs in its own try/catch: a release that throws does not replace the original error (the original surfaces, with the release failure attached as cause), the conflict and source-fingerprint paths still RETURN their failed receipt rather than throwing, and the task and milestone releases are attempted separately so one failure cannot skip the other

releaseIdBlock no longer matches on id plus family alone: an entry written by a different run that happens to carry the same id and family survives, because the match uses the entries the reservation wrote or a run identity
migration_approval_digest_mismatch carries the same re-preview hint as migration_id_block_moved with its exit code unchanged, and both error names appear in the CHANGELOG entry and in the guide
releaseIdBlock has unit tests covering a same-family entry with another id surviving, another family entry surviving, and a null common directory returning false and writing nothing

The lock-timeout hint no longer addresses a create-only audience at a site reachable from migration, the task record-directory list exists in one place rather than two, and the milestone marker is passed through instead of hardcoded
